survey: Stone checkers/chess table set in a park, seen from above at three-quarter view. Main parts: (1) a thick square stone tabletop with a raised rim and an inset 5x5 grid of dark and cream tiles. The tiles lie flat inside the rim with dark squares in all four corners. (2) One square stone pedestal under the centre of the top. Its upper end meets the top's underside and its lower end stands on (3) a flat square stone base slab, which lies on the grass with grass tufts along its edges. (4) Two round stone stools shaped like mushrooms: a domed cap on a slightly tapering drum. The front-right stool stands on the grass with grass around its foot. The rear-left stool is partly hidden behind the tabletop, which overlaps it in the right depth order. Its foot also sits in the grass. The stool caps are ellipses that fit the camera's viewing angle. The tool marked no thin parts, ends or branches, and there are no cables or rigging. Every part rests on something: top on pedestal, pedestal on slab, slab and stools on the ground. The 5x5 board is a simplified game board, not a construction fault.
